headline: DOE, MARINA and BFP Move to Develop EV Ferry Safety Rules After June Aster Fire
seoTitle: DOE, MARINA, BFP Develop EV Ferry Safety Rules After June Aster Fire | FMB News
seoDescription: The Energy Department says it is coordinating with MARINA and the BFP on rules for carrying electric and hybrid vehicles aboard ships after the deadly MV June Aster fire.
deck: Government agencies are developing clearer rules for carrying electric and hybrid vehicles aboard Philippine vessels. Investigators have not established that the EV aboard MV June Aster caused the September 9 fire.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead as Search Continues
continuesFrom.whatChanged: The response to the September 9 ferry disaster has moved into regulation: DOE says it is coordinating with MARINA and BFP on EV and lithium-ion battery safety standards for vessels, while a domestic ferry operator has imposed an immediate company-level EV and hybrid vehicle ban.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Energy said Thursday that it is coordinating with the Maritime Industry Authority and Bureau of Fire Protection to develop clearer safety rules covering electric vehicles, hybrid vehicles and lithium-ion batteries, including their carriage aboard Philippine vessels.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the agencies are working toward standards intended to protect passengers and vessels while allowing electric mobility to continue. The DOE is also participating in work on the 2026 implementing rules and regulations of the Fire Code to address emerging EV and battery risks.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The regulatory work follows the September 9 MV June Aster fire off Coron, Palawan. DOE Energy Utilization Management Bureau Director Patrick Aquino told senators that existing regulations do not specifically prohibit transporting EVs and that DOE is coordinating with MARINA on specific guidance for shipping lines.

Montenegro Shipping Lines separately announced an immediate company-level ban on electric and hybrid vehicles aboard its vessels, for both passenger and cargo carriage. DOE described the operator's temporary restriction as a prudent safety step while broader standards are being developed.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Authorities have not determined that the electric vehicle carried aboard MV June Aster caused the fire. The vessel also carried other vehicles and cargo, and the official investigation remains ongoing.
FMB News is therefore not presenting the presence of an EV, survivor accounts of an explosion, or the new regulatory response as proof of the fire's origin or cause.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Inter-island shipping is a core part of Philippine passenger and cargo transport. A uniform national standard would affect ferry operators, EV and hybrid owners, logistics companies, ports and regulators across an archipelagic transport network.

The policy question also sits at the intersection of maritime safety and the government's push for electric mobility: rules must account for battery-fire risks without assuming an unproven cause in the June Aster disaster.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: DOE and MARINA have not yet issued the final nationwide vessel-carriage rules described in Thursday's statements. The scope, technical requirements, inspection procedures and implementation date remain to be finalized.
The Philippine Coast Guard, MARINA, BFP and DOE continue work related to the June Aster investigation. A final official finding on the fire's cause has not been issued.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal MARINA and DOE issuances setting national EV and hybrid-vehicle carriage requirements, the final 2026 Fire Code implementing rules, whether other ferry operators adopt temporary restrictions, and the investigating agencies' formal findings on the June Aster fire.

verificationNotes: PNA reports a September 17 DOE statement confirming coordination with BFP on the 2026 Fire Code IRR and with MARINA on vessel-carriage protocols for EVs and hybrids.

GMA independently reports DOE Energy Utilization Management Bureau Director Patrick Aquino's Senate statement that existing rules do not specifically prohibit EV carriage and that specific regulations are being developed with MARINA.
Power Philippines independently reports the DOE's coordination with MARINA, BFP and the Philippine Coast Guard and the stated goal of clear, science-based and uniform requirements.
GMA reports Montenegro Shipping Lines' company statement imposing an immediate EV and HEV ban. The article distinguishes this private operator restriction from a nationwide government prohibition.
No verified source reviewed establishes that the EV aboard MV June Aster caused the fire. The article explicitly preserves that unresolved status.

The hero photograph is the same genuinely relevant Philippine Coast Guard file image previously rights-verified by FMB News on Wikimedia Commons as PD-PhilippinesGov. Its caption does not imply that the photograph proves fire causation.

This is a continuation of FMB News' earliest September 10 June Aster report because the independently newsworthy change is the emergence of a concrete interagency regulatory response after the disaster.
